title: Data Skew: One Holding Account for 80,000 Contacts

steps.prompt: Integration jobs attach every unmatched Contact to one Unassigned Account, which now has 80,000 Contacts. When the jobs insert Contacts in parallel, many inserts fail with UNABLE_TO_LOCK_ROW on that Account. How should the architect change the design?

options.label: Spread unmatched Contacts round-robin across a pool of holding Accounts
options.rationale: Past about 10,000 children a single parent becomes a lock hotspot under concurrent operations. Keeping each holding parent under that threshold lets parallel jobs lock different Account rows.

options.label: Sort each integration batch by AccountId before loading
options.rationale: Sorting by parent Id stops concurrent batches from contending across many parents, but every Contact here shares one parent, so each batch still locks the same Account row.

options.label: Reassign the holding Account to an owner who has no role
options.rationale: A role-free owner reduces sharing recalculation for ownership skew, but each Contact insert still locks the one parent Account.
